content:
When Apple finally responded to the sharp rise in the cost of memory and other components, the company held nothing back. Some price increases were over 50%, and some memory and storage upgrades simply doubled in price.

These higher prices are likely to persist for years, and may never come down……

9to5Mac readers were already skeptical about whether Apple would reduce prices even after component shortages eased. Over two-thirds of readers said they expected the price increases to be permanent.

A subsequent analyst report noted that supply chain pricing would not improve in any meaningful way before 2028, and even then only marginally. As things stand, these steep price hikes look set to last at least several years, and quite possibly forever.

Assuming that is indeed the case, how would you respond? Would you grit your teeth and continue buying Apple products at the same rate? Would you cut back on the number or frequency of Apple purchases? Or would you take other measures, such as buying lower-tier models, picking up refurbished units, or waiting for discounts?

Please take part in our poll, and share your thoughts in the comments. The poll allows multiple selections, in case you plan to change your spending behaviour in more than one way.
